title: Mathematical Foundations of TITAN PACK — 2D Strip Packing & MILP Linearization
lead: Explore the Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation of 2D Strip / Bin Packing behind TITAN PACK, along with the multi-scale interlocking algorithms that guarantee zero-fault-line solutions.
sec1P1: The 2D Packing Problem is a combinatorial optimization challenge where rectangular parts of various dimensions must be placed inside a bounding sheet or plate without overlapping or exceeding boundary limits. It has extensive real-world applications in sheet-metal manufacturing, woodworking, cutting-stock layouts, and VLSI floorplanning.
sec1P2: Deciding whether a set of items can be packed with zero scrap (100% material efficiency) without void is known to be strongly NP-hard.

warnTitle: Choice of Big-M and Numerical Stability
warnBody: Setting Big-M to an arbitrary large number can weaken the continuous LP relaxation bound, increasing the number of branch-and-bound nodes. It may also trigger numerical instability where parts slightly overlap within solver tolerances ($10^{-6}$) and are falsely treated as feasible. Setting tight, provable upper bounds ($M_x = W$ and $M_y = H$) is standard practice in mathematical programming.
sec3P1: If a rectangle is naively sliced with full-width or full-height cuts, continuous fault lines (guillotine cuts) emerge, degrading structural rigidity and breaking the puzzle into trivial independent sub-puzzles.
sec3P2: TITAN PACK uses a Multi-Scale Interlocking & Core Partitioning algorithm that guarantees every interior grid line $c \in \{1, \dots, W-1\}$ and $r \in \{1, \dots, H-1\}$ is crossed by at least one overlapping metal girder ($x_i < c < x_i + w_i$), ensuring an interlocking puzzle with zero continuous fault lines (furthermore, when identical parts exist, adding symmetry-breaking constraints like $x_i \le x_j$ eliminates redundant permutation branches in solver search).
